title: Suppressing Majorana Hybridization in Atomically Assembled Cr Chains on Bi2Pd
authors: Jinkyung Kim, Piotr Kot, Ryo Ogawa, Atustaka Maeda, Andreas J. Heinrich, Nicolas Lorente, Deung-Jang Choi
abstract: Magnetic-atom chains on superconductors can host Majorana zero modes, but in finite chains the two end modes generally hibridize and split away from zero energy. We show that Cr chains assembled atom-by-atom on the Bi-terminated surface of Bi2Pd enter a short-localization-length Shiba chain regime wthat strongly suppreesses this finite-size hybridization. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals a chaing-leght-driven closing and reopening of the in-gap spectrum, followed by zero-bias modes localized at the chains ends. Green-function calculations reproduce the evolution and show an exchange of electorn-holec haracter across the transition. From the residual splitting we extract a localization length of about three atomic sites, explaining the stability of the zero-energy modes in experimentally accessible chains.
summary: This research reports on the assembly of magnetic Cr chains on a superconducting $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Pd}$ surface to study Majorana zero modes. By combining STM measurements and advanced Green's function theory, the authors demonstrate that the hybridization of end modes is strongly suppressed, evidenced by a measurable, short localization length. This work advances the feasibility of using engineered superconducting heterostructures for topological quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary goal is to demonstrate and theoretically explain the suppression of Majorana zero mode (MZM) hybridization in finite magnetic-atom chains assembled on a superconducting surface.
main_result: The experiment shows a chain-length-driven evolution of the in-gap spectrum, and calculations extract a short localization length ($\xi_M \approx 3$ sites), confirming the stability of zero-energy end modes.
method: The study combines scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STM) measurements of the local density of states (LDOS) with theoretical modeling using Green's function calculations (Bogoliubov-de Gennes formalism).
model_or_system: The system involves Cr magnetic atoms assembled into chains on the Bi-terminated surface of the superconductor $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Pd}$. The physics is modeled using impurity Hamiltonians within the Nambu Green's function framework.
key_observables: In-gap spectrum evolution (YSR state closing/reopening), zero-bias conductance localized at chain ends, and the extracted Majorana localization length ($\xi_M$).
important_parameters: The localization length ($\xi_M \approx 10.5 	ext{ \AA}$ or $\sim 3$ sites), the superconducting gap ($\Delta_{	ext{topo}} \approx 204 \mu	ext{eV}$), and the Rashba coupling ($\alpha_R$).
main_assumptions: The interpretation assumes that the observed zero-bias peaks are indeed Majorana-like end states, and theoretical calculations rely on the dilute-impurity framework.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the length-controlled gap closing/reopening via $	ext{d}I/	ext{d}V$ maps, the concentration of zero-bias spectral weight at the ends, and spin-resolved LDOS showing spin texture evolution.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of presenting experimental observations (STM measurements of $	ext{d}I/	ext{d}V$ vs. chain length) which are then explained and quantified using detailed theoretical calculations (Green's functions, localization length extraction, and analysis of coupling variations).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally realized platform for studying topological superconductivity, directly addressing the critical issue of finite-size effects on Majorana modes, which is highly relevant to quantum computing hardware.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Schematic of the STM junction used to assemble and probe Cr spin chains on the superconducting β-Bi2Pd surface. The experiment combines atom-by-atom construc- tion with local tunnelling spectroscopy to follow the finite-size evolution of Shiba-chain end modes. (b) Atomic structure of the chains, with Cr adatoms aligned along the ⟨110⟩direction of the Bi-terminated surface. The surface consists of a top Bi layer, followed by Pd and Bi layers stacked along the z axis. (c–f) Constant-current STM images of Cr4, Cr5, Cr8, and Cr12 chains assembled atom by atom. STM parameters: V = 3 mV, I = 50 pA, scan area 5 × 5 nm2.

FIG. 2. (a) Spatially resolved differential-conductance maps acquired along Crx chains with x = 4, 5, 8, 12, plotted as a function of position along the chain and applied bias. (b) Computed LDOS showing the same qualitative evolution with increasing chain length as in the experiment in (a): the in-gap YSR states approach zero energy for Cr4, the Shiba-band gap closes near Cr5, and a gap reopens for longer chains. In Cr12, the reopened gap is accompanied by zero-bias resonances localized near the two chain ends. This length-controlled closing and reopening of the gap marks the entrance into the confined Shiba-chain regime whose localization length is quantified in Fig. 4.

Figure 4 addresses this point for the Cr12 chain. A constant-current profile over the chain is shown in Fig. 4(a), while Fig. 4(b) shows the corresponding zero- bias conductance profile along the same chain. The spec- tral weight is concentrated near the two ends and is strongly reduced in the central region, indicating com- pact end-localized modes. The calculation for an ideal chain of identical Cr atoms [Fig. 4(c)] gives nearly mirror- symmetric zero-energy profiles at the two ends. However, the experimental profile in (b) displays a clear imbalance between the two edge amplitudes.

FIG. 3. (a) Calculated in-gap transverse spin component ⟨Sx⟩for Crx chains with x = 4, 5, 8, 12, plotted as a func- tion of position and energy. Short chains display alternat- ing transverse spin contrast induced by the strong surface spin–orbit coupling. For Cr8 and Cr12, the zero-energy spec- tral weight develops opposite-sign transverse spin features localized near the two chain ends, consistent with the for- mation of symmetry-related end modes. (b) The longitudi- nal spin component ⟨Sz⟩show predominantly ferromagnetic alignment, with spin-down and spin-up character associated with electron-like and hole-like branches, respectively. (b) Zero-bias differential conductance dI/dV (V = 0) measured along the same chain, showing spectral weight lo- calized near the two ends and a reduced signal in the central region.
